formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: The signature lets anyone who submits it call permit, which sets the spender's allowance over the owner's AERO to exactly `value`. This replaces any earlier allowance and does not add to it.
The allowance can be spent with transferFrom until it is used up. At type(uint256).max it never goes down.
The signature is valid only up to `deadline` (block.timestamp <= deadline) and only for the owner's current nonce, which permit uses up.
No tokens move and no native value is sent when the message is signed.
formats.shown: "Authorize spending of tokens", with the spender as a raw address, the max spending amount in AERO ("Unlimited" at or above 2^255), the owner and a 'Valid until' date. The nonce is hidden.

findings.title: Permit has no test case, so no rendering of the amount, the Unlimited message or the date is checked.
findings.evidence: FORMATS.md: 'cases: 0 (no tx)' for Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline).
findings.fix: Add one test with a finite AERO value and one with value = type(uint256).max, so the 'Unlimited' message is rendered.

findings.title: The Permit intent says 'tokens' but not AERO, and does not name the spender or the amount.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: "intent": "Authorize spending of tokens"; Aero.sol constructor ERC20("Aerodrome", "AERO"); ERC20Permit.permit calls _approve(owner, spender, value).
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Allow spending of your AERO". Consider an interpolatedIntent: "Allow {spender} to spend up to {value}".

findings.title: The Permit spender uses the raw format, so the wallet does not try to resolve a name for the address.
